reading.body:
Tecnodati S.R.L. is an unverified OpenStreetMap record, not a confirmed data center, and it carries no capacity figure at all.

The entry is a single node tagged telecom=data_center near Parma, Italy, with a name that reads as a plausible small Italian IT or data-services company. The research note is explicit that no operator website, press coverage, or business registration was confirmed, and that the search quota ran out before verification could happen. The only source is a tagging review. So the record's existence in the dataset reflects a map edit, not a demonstrated facility.

For AI infrastructure this matters as a caution about the bottom of the supply chain. The binding constraints on AI scaling are power and buildings, and those constraints are measured in megawatts and grid interconnects. This record reports zero megawatts, which is the absence of a measurement rather than a small one. A name containing "dati" is not evidence of compute, and a map tag is not evidence of a building.

What the data does not tell you is whether any facility exists here, how large it is, or whether it serves AI workloads at all. It also does not establish that Italy's data-center inventory is small or large, because this is one unconfirmed node among many. The honest reading is that this is a lead awaiting verification, and that any count of data centers built from OpenStreetMap alone will include entries like it.
